issues.description: The Latin has a single accusative object, 'eum, qui fecerat mare' (him who had made the sea), as the object of 'separat'. There is no pronoun corresponding to 'them'; the translator has introduced an extra party ('them') not present in the Latin.

issues.span: does not separate them from him who had made the sea
issues.description: The Latin means 'the sea does not separate him who had made the sea' — 'eum qui fecerat mare' is a single referent serving as the direct object of 'separat' (subject 'mare'). The English splits 'eum' and 'qui' into two distinct entities ('them' vs. 'him who had made the sea'), changing the grammatical structure and the sense.
